text:
ConocoPhillips rose slightly today as crude oil prices remained elevated despite recent volatility. U.S. oil is trading near $97 per barrel and world oil near $110, supported by escalating Middle East tensions—Saudi Arabia shut down a major pipeline after drone attacks this week, and Houthi militants have advanced to control a key Red Sea island that threatens the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a critical chokepoint for global oil shipments. Even though oil prices fell on Friday after their multiday rally, the underlying geopolitical risk keeps a floor under energy prices.

The stock has climbed 6% over two weeks as these supply disruption concerns have built. For an oil producer like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices directly improve profitability, so the combination of tighter global supply and persistent Middle East instability works in the company's favor even as financial markets digest which way the crisis will ultimately move prices.
